articles.title: An Iconic Piece Of Gaming Artwork Just Fetched A Princely Sum At Auction
articles.summary: If you were an arcade operator 45 years ago, your first look at a game that would change the history of the medium came in the form of a humble sales flyer. On the front was a detailed cartoon illustration that envisioned the game's premise: an ape throwing barrels down scaffolding, a terrified…
body: That now-legendary artwork, made to sell the game cabinet to skeptical arcade owners, was among a host of Nintendo memorabilia that went up for auction today -- and it sold for almost $330,000, more than doubling its estimated final bid price.

The Donkey Kong flyer artwork, done by legendary illustrator Leslie Carbaga, is of significant historical importance. It would go on to make numerous appearances across Donkey Kong-related merchandise over the decades and help establish the initial appearance of Mario and DK in early media like the Saturday Supercade cartoon. But, according to former Nintendo advertising director Donna Darbous -- whose collection this piece comes from -- it was originally slated for a dumpster when a storage room was being cleaned out to make office space. Recognizing the value of this and other art being stored, Darbous took it home and stored it away, only uncovering it again recently.

articles.title: Kane Parsons Confirms Meetings With Valve, But Won't Adapt Their Games If It Can't Be Done Right
articles.summary: Backrooms director Kane Parsons has confirmed his meetings with Valve, but says that he has no plans to adapt any of their games if it can't be done well. When speaking on an October 28 episode of The Kyle Buchanan Show, Parsons wore a Valve hoodie, which prompted Buchanan to inquire about Parsons'…
body: "They work in experiments, and I like that, because that tends to be how I work," he said. "I don't have a desire to sensationalize anything I may or may not be talking to them about over there, because it's mainly: Is it possible to make something compelling in some way that we like? What do you guys want to do? What do I want to do? Is there anything on the table in any way, shape, or form?

"And if it's not, I would defend a future where we don't even go down that road, but it's more like having an abstract creative conversation that could flow in like 30 different directions. If you know the way Valve works, I think they're looking to experiment more internally than anything that's going to be talked about. If something cool comes of it, I am sure somehow, people will know."

As noted, Parsons has expressed interest in making a Portal movie and also recently confirmed that he is working on three "dream projects." These projects seem to be linked to some kind of IP, but Parsons has also previously stated he has no real interest in a property like Star Wars, and his desire for adaptations lies more within a small handful of things from his childhood, such as Valve's games.

articles.title: James Gunn Confirms Batman and Wonder Woman Are 'Diamond Characters' in the DCU Despite Their Continued Absence
articles.summary: James Gunn has clarified DC Studios’ 8-10 year roadmap and confirmed its focus on Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman as its “diamond characters.” Gunn shared this information on Threads in response to a now-deleted post, where he urged the original poster to study up on his quotes from January 2023…
body: “I said some stories would be standalone like the Guardians movies were (which is what Clayface is), and some stories would have part of a larger narrative structure, which is what the Superman Saga is. All that said, each piece of the larger story should work on its own with or without having to see everything else,” he said.

He went on to clarify that the “often-cited 8-10 year roadmap” for the DCU doesn’t just apply to story points, but also outlines the plan for “DC as a whole.” This includes focusing on “diamond characters,” which Gunn confirmed are, perhaps unsurprisingly, Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman, as well as “smaller characters we could turn into diamonds.” These smaller characters were listed as Krypto the Superdog, John Stewart, and Peacemaker.
According to Gunn, this plan also factors in how DC will “foster filmmaker freedom and allow for multiple tones and ratings, the influences of Star Wars and George R.R. Martin, and so much more."
“It's exciting seeing things start to come together, and all that makes me even more excited for what we have in store for everyone in Man of Tomorrow,” he said.

articles.title: GTA 6 Online Could Be Released In Early 2027, Bank Says
articles.summary: Take-Two's biggest release ever, GTA 6, is coming up in November, but the company's share price continues to drop. It's down 21% this year and has now dipped under $200 this week after reaching a 52-week high of $265.
body: In short, the stock is struggling, but one big bank says it sees a lot of upside, in part because Rockstar is expected to release a new version of GTA Online--potentially in the first quarter of 2027--that could generate loads of money.

"We recommend being long $TTWO through the GTA 6 launch," the bank said in a memo to investors seen by Business Insider. Being "long" means the investor would buy and hold. The bank said Take-Two stock "remains cheap."

In particular, Bank of America said investors are not fully appreciating how big GTA Online 2.0 could be. To be sure, Rockstar is calling GTA 6 a single-player game, but everyone expects multiplayer to arrive in some form eventually. GTA Online for GTA 5 has been, and continues to be, a huge moneymaker for Rockstar and Take-Two thanks to its many microtransactions. Many expect a new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 to up the ante even further and give players more reasons to spend time--and money--in the game.

Bank of America said a new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 could launch in the first calendar quarter of 2027, meaning January-March. This is also around the time that a PC edition of GTA 6 could arrive, driving even more revenue.

articles.title: LOTRO’s Latest Expansion Is Out Now, Nearly 20 Years After The Game Launched
articles.summary: The Lord of the Rings Online, an MMO based on the popular fantasy series, got its latest expansion today, some 19.5 years after the game was originally released in 2007.
body: The new expansion is called The Wolves of Mordor, and as its name suggests, the expansion is focused on the werewolves of Mordor who are going after the people who took down their master, Sauron.

The expansion takes players beyond Gorgoroth where they will "gather unlikely allies and uncover the secrets hidden in Mordor's forgotten corners." Players will visit three new regions: Heledhris, Parth Rhavas, and Nan Ogol. In those places, players can learn new skills and receive enhancements, and then mix and match them to create a unique playstyle.

The Wolves of Mordor expansion also adds new companions called Neighbors, who have their own unique personality traits and a "dynamic mood system." Players can forge friendships with these companions, and the companions can tell the player stories, provide gifts, and send them on missions.

The Wolves of Mordor is available in a $40 standard edition, an $80 Collector's Edition with extra cosmetics, and the $130 Ultimate Fan Bundle. This version comes with even more cosmetics, additional neighbor characters, and XP boosts, among other things.

articles.title: WoW: Forever Content Updates Will Come Slower Than You Might Expect
articles.summary: Developer Blizzard's new version of its flagship MMORPG, World of Warcraft: Forever, will receive content updates "every four months," avoiding modern WoW's somewhat controversial eight-week patch cycle.
body: In an interview with IGN, Forever principal game designer Kris Zierhut revealed the content schedule plan and explained Blizzard's reasoning. He said WoW Classic's Season of Discovery received updates "way too fast," every 8-10 weeks.

Since the launch of WoW's Dragonflight expansion in 2022, an eight-week update schedule is also what modern WoW operates on. Its more frequent patch schedule means there's always something new to do, but has been criticized by some players due to the buggy nature of recent updates and lackluster content.

On the other hand, some older expansions, like Warlords of Draenor and Shadowlands, saw content droughts that lasted six months or more, leaving players hungry for something new to do. Forever will split the difference.
"We're fairly convinced the correct [update] rate is something closer to once every four months or 17 weeks or three times a year," Zierhut said.

articles.title: The Case Against Larian Saving Dragon Age, No Matter How Tempting It Sounds
articles.summary: The possible takeover is hardly a new idea. Fans have been asking Larian to move into Thedas — Dragon Age’s world, a continent of grudging nations and grim cathedrals and a god nobody can quite prove is real — since Baldur’s Gate 3 came out in 2023 and completely rewrote the rules of fantasy RPG…
body: The same day Bloomberg broke the news that EA was closing BioWare, one semi-viral post on X neatly summarized the feelings of some fans: The Mass Effect IP should go to CD Projekt Red, Dragon Age to Larian Studios, and Dead Space to Capcom (not BioWare’s in the first place, but the poster was on a roll). Listen: I understand where this is coming from. I adore Larian. I love (most of) the Dragon Age games. I know that bargaining is one of the stages of grief. And I also firmly believe — I am so sorry — that Larian should stay far, far away from Dragon Age.

In 2024, the studio said that after six years in the Forgotten Realms, it was ready to “ seize this opportunity to develop our own IPs.” That opportunity now has a name: Divinity, announced at The Game Awards in December 2025 as a game even larger than Baldur’s Gate 3. Asking Larian to take on Thedas means asking it to set its dream project down.

articles.title: Epic Games further doubles down on gen-AI tools for Fortnite, Unreal Engine 6 and more: "Our engineers are no longer writing the bulk of the code"
articles.summary: To no one's surprise, Epic Games has now confirmed that it's tripling down on its gen-AI push and will use the controversial tech on everything from Fortnite to the next iteration of its widely-used game development engine, Unreal Engine 6.
body: Speaking to This Week In Video Games, executive vice president of development Marcus Wassmer confirmed that "we are definitely using AI to develop code and features for Unreal Engine," but that work will also be extended to the engine's next big numbered version. "Almost all development happening right now is being done in the dev streams attached to Fortnite, UEFN [Unreal Editor for Fortnite], and UE6."

When asked specifically if Epic is vibe-coding anything related to Unreal Engine, Wassmer put it plainly: "Yes, we are vibe-coding things. That means our engineers are no longer writing the bulk of the code, but they are still guiding the tools to get the architectural result we want. We're not 'one-shotting' the engine; we're iterating with AI to ship features developers want and keep the engine within the memory, performance, and scalability envelopes." Wassmer claimed the AI tools would help the company push out updates faster and with fewer bugs.

articles.title: BG3 Owes Everything to One Underrated 2009 BioWare RPG
articles.summary: It’s late. The fire is burning low. The sardonic elven rogue who joined your party a few days ago pulls up a log, flashes a grin, and tells you (cheerfully) about his former employer, who would love to see him dead. The elf flirts with you like it’s a survival skill.
body: If you’ve picked up a controller in the last three years, you know exactly who this is: Astarion, the beloved disaster from Baldur’s Gate 3. Plot twist: Wrong game, wrong decade. This is Zevran — Zev, to his friends — from Dragon Age: Origins, released by BioWare in 2009. He’s been hired to kill you, so your meetcute could be deadly. Proceed with caution.

Origins is a dark fantasy RPG that many tend to overlook because of its age. It’s got dated graphics (the game is so very beige) and glitches galore. But, if you’re a fan of Baldur’s Gate 3 and you’ve got about 50 hours to spare, there is no better use of your time than meeting and falling in love with Origins ’ merry band of misfits — and experiencing the well-written, responsive world of Thedas for the first time. You’re going to see some similarities. BioWare’s co-founders themselves have described Dragon Age as a spiritual successor to their own Baldur’s Gate series, and there’s quite a lot that Baldur’s Gate 3 and Origins, specifically, have in common.

articles.title: Alien: Isolation 2 devs commit to a physical edition: "Staying true to the analogue nature of Alien is one of our pillars"
articles.summary: The developers behind Alien: Isolation 2 are committing to a full physical edition, and have shared even more details about the highly-anticipated survival horror sequel.
body: In a recent developer Q&A posted today (below), developers from Creative Assembly shed even more light on their shadowy follow-up to 2014's fan-favorite horror game. When asked if the sequel would get a physical edition, the devs simply said "yes" and explained that "staying true to the analogue nature of Alien is one of our pillars."

Throughout the video, the Creative Assembly team reiterated that so much of their inspiration comes from Ridley Scott's seminal sci-fi classic from 1979, naturally, which influenced their decision to release a physical boxed version of the game and to keep the focus on one ever present, highly intelligent and always frightening Xenomorph.

Confirmation of a physical release comes months after Sony announced plans to end production of new PlayStation discs in 2028 - a decision that led to heated backlash from players, physical distributors and consumer rights groups.

articles.title: Backrooms Director Teases Next Dream Projects — Is Portal One of Them?
articles.summary: Since the buzzy horror film Backrooms propelled Kane Parsons to instant fame, many are eager to know what the young director is working on next. Beyond a confirmed Backrooms sequel, many are convinced he will bring another world of corporate drudgery to the screen: it seems quite possible he'll…
body: He said in a May interview with The New York Times that working on a Portal film would be his “dream.” Given how popular Parsons is right now, this situation has unsurprisingly led to speculation that he may be gearing up to make a Portal film. Official confirmation seems distant, but a recent interview has made it tempting to connect certain dots.

In a clip posted yesterday by podcaster Kyle Buchanan, Parsons says that he is currently working on “three dream projects.” He jokes that if he specifies further, “they’ll get me with their space lasers.” The director clarifies that these dream projects are still early on, and that he’s still “in an information phase.” The cherry on top: he’s wearing a Valve hoodie during the interview.

While this tidbit may seem circumstantial on its own, the idea that Parsons is working on a Portal movie feels more plausible in the broader context. According to his own Instagram stories, the director has visited Valve at least twice this year: once in June and again this September. Parsons has been teasing some sort of collaboration with the Portal developer, and posted a picture of a valve in the orientation of the company’s logo on Instagram.

articles.title: Resident Evil Lead Teases Series’ ‘Conclusion’ Coming In the Next 10 Years
articles.summary: Resident Evil is celebrating its 30th anniversary this year. Capcom's iconic horror series has been a foundational part of the survival horro genre, and it's still delivering amazing entries, such as this year's Resident Evil Requiem. Still, that doesn't mean it will be around forever.
body: In an interview with Yahoo Japan, executive producer Jun Takeuchi teased that the Resident Evil franchise's overarching narrative could come to an end shockingly soon. Takeuchi called Requiem the end of Capcom's original ten-year plan for the series that originated during planning stages for the Resident Evil 2 remake. Looking forward, he revealed that, "I think the conclusion will come in the next 10 years" (via machine translation). In that timeframe, Takeuchi said there will be multiple titles for fans to look forward to.

What that conclusion actually looks like is hard to guess. It feels wild to believe that Capcom would truly put an end to Resident Evil. Perhaps the "conclusion" Takeuchi talked about has to do with the characters and narrative arcs the series is currently focused on. Requiem itself felt like a survey of the series' past and present, bringing back familiar faces like Leon Kennedy. Perhaps there is a world in which we get a fresh start or a complete reboot. Capcom almost did something like that with Resident Evil 7, which served as a soft reboot but still had connections to past games.

Players will explore the dark narrative of a man turning against the Collective to grab hold of a lost Essence.
Take on new enemies, harness new abilities, and uncover the next chapter.
Cronos: Lazarus is launching on December 3 for PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox Series X|S, and PC (Steam, GOG, and Epic Games Store), with a release coming soon to Nintendo Switch 2.

videos.title: Floor Plan: Slap Out Of It! – Announcement Trailer – Nintendo Switch 2
videos.summary: Floor Plan: Slap Out Of It! lands on Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch in spring 2027!
body: Floor Plan: Slap Out Of It! is a slap-and-solve adventure that stretches your wits and your noodly arms to the max. Hop in an elevator and search for lost relics in an impossible office tower, a vertical sandbox of secrets filled with absurd escape room-style puzzles that will keep you thinking and laughing at the same time. Everything within reach of your stretchy arms is satisfyingly interactive and responsive to your touch, so explore and slap everything. You never know what might happen!
Visit Nintendo.com for more info:
